It's clear Voat is growing incredibly rapidly. And as the latest down page mentioned Atko has already been engaged with multiple venture capital firms looking to get a piece of the site. I know I wasn't the only one who immediately felt a bit uneasy about that. The problem is that as soon as money gets involved things start to get twisted.

Can we thus layout the site's principles in a sort of site constitution? It'd be a short plain English document that is an agreement between the site and its users. A sort of reverse terms and conditions. We'd have to discuss exactly what should be in it, but for instance I think an obvious one would be an agreement for the site to never engage in native advertising or complicity towards such things. Anything that is sponsored or otherwise generating revenue for the site would be clearly marked as purchased content. Another would be a formal declaration of what has been repeatedly said - No content will ever be removed by administration unless it's presence is illegal according to the laws of the country hosting this site. And so on.

We'd need some public sort of way of amending or changing things in the constitution, but in general it'd be a big step forward. It'd also allow people to more readily answer the question of, "Well what makes you think Voat isn't just going to turn into [that other site]?"
Should Voat create a site constitution to clarify what will or will not ever be done on this site?

No. I think they should let Voat evolve into whatever it may. The Admins should have their own constitution, to remind them to never make the same mistakes Reddit has, but let the users be free to pioneer this place.

The constitution would be exclusively to guide the actions of the admins. It's a more clear and formal statement for the users of how they will be treated on this site. I have complete faith in Atko trying to do the right thing, but if venture capital gets their hands on this site things are going to change. The goal is for users to know what will not change.
